title: AI-generated, playable 2D shooter-style abilities, gamemodes, and world elements
author: 77LuckyLucky7
selftext:
I've noticed that there are several popular shooter games, but people sometimes complain about recycled mechanics and eventually getting bored of them, such as Brawl Stars. With AI coding becoming more capable and sandbox games like Minecraft remaining popular, I wondered: **What if AI could generate playable game elements based on any concept?**

I made 3 single-player sandboxes experimenting with this idea: one for abilities, one for gamemodes, and one for world elements. I built them through vibe-coding, testing, and brainstorming improvements to fix bugs and add more versatility so it can create things more diversely. There's probably still plenty of things to improve, but I think they're functional enough to share.

Rather than letting AI generate code, each sandbox gives it a set of primitives that it can combine into short, functional scripts. All 3 of these sandboxes save these scripts to local storage based on what they're designed to generate:  
  
1. Ability Sandbox: Create abilities containing functionality for projectiles, area effects, spawnables, wall & bush interactions, and conditional modifiers.

2. Gamemode Sandbox: Create gamemodes involving objectives, areas, collectables, spawnables, and destination points. Teammates and enemies are controlled by bots.

3. World Sandbox: This one has 3 different features.  
\- Create tiles including obstacles, hazards, zones, and status effect tiles.  
\- Create entities with distinct targeting, spawning, moving, and status effect behaviors.  
\- Create regimes, which are essentially 1-player minigames with objectives such as destroying entities, painting the world's grid, or navigating around a wall of enemies to reach a finish line.

I'm also curious how interesting these systems could potentially become if they were eventually combined into one multiplayer sandbox where AI-generated abilities, gamemodes, and worlds could all interact with each other.
